courier-relay/protocol-versioning: Courier Relay protocol versioning (main.py), current as of issue trial-0o0 (2026-09-07): CURRENT_PROTOCOL="2" and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS=("1", "2"). The provider permanently adopted protocol 2 and the integration owner approved it as current. An omitted "protocol" in a request selects CURRENT_PROTOCOL ("2"); an explicit supported version selects that version and stays supported after a newer current version is introduced ("1" remains supported). Commands count, summary, and accepted share analyze(q), which returns (protocol, receipts, accepted_list) and dispatches on version via accepted_receipts(protocol, receipts); accepted_list is None for an unsupported version, and every command then returns {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. count and summary share receipt_counts() and return exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count} reporting the protocol actually used. accepted (issue trial-zee) returns exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, receipts}: the counts equal summary for the same request, and receipts holds the accepted representatives selected under the chosen protocol, unchanged (fields, timestamp spelling, payload) and in original input order; empty input gives receipts [] and zero counts; a single receipt is returned unchanged. Issue trial-0o0 (integration partner export) confirmed accepted with explicit "protocol":"1" uses the original protocol 1 contract (identity and representative rule below) with the same response shape and input order; omitted protocol still selects "2". Per-version rules: protocol 1 = accepted_receipts_v1, contract in vendor/protocol-1.md: identity=(account_id, delivery_id), same delivery_id under different accounts is a separate delivery; accept EARLIEST occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point. Protocol 2 = accepted_receipts_v2, contract in vendor/protocol-2.md: identity=delivery_id alone across all accounts, same ID under another account is another receipt of the same delivery; accept LATEST occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point. Both keep accepted receipts unchanged in original input order; the rule applies to the whole supplied set regardless of receipt dates. Timestamps parsed via parse_instant() (RFC3339, Z or numeric offset, compared as UTC). When adding protocol N: add accepted_receipts_vN plus vendor/protocol-N.md, add its branch in accepted_receipts() so count, summary, and accepted all pick it up, add N to SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS, and change CURRENT_PROTOCOL only when N becomes current. Public suites name protocols explicitly; run python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/<file>.json (accepted_1.json, accepted_2.json, count_1.json, summary_1.json, summary_2.json); regression tests in tests/ (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests; test_accepted.py covers accepted for both protocols, class AcceptedProtocol1 covers explicit protocol 1). Earlier state preserved under key courier-relay/protocol-versioning-history-protocol-1-current. Source: issues trial-vbm, trial-dvi, trial-u7q, trial-zee, trial-0o0; vendor/protocol-1.md, vendor/protocol-2.md.
courier-relay/protocol-versioning-histor: HISTORICAL (superseded 2026-09-07 by issue trial-u7q, which made protocol 2 current; see courier-relay/protocol-versioning for the standing agreement). Courier Relay protocol versioning as of issues trial-vbm and trial-dvi (main.py): CURRENT_PROTOCOL="1" and SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS=("1",). An omitted "protocol" in a request selects CURRENT_PROTOCOL; an explicit supported version selects that version and stays supported after a newer current version is introduced. Commands count (original single-account use) and summary (cross-account batch, issue trial-dvi) share one body, receipt_counts(), which returns exactly {protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count} and dispatches on version via accepted_receipts(protocol, receipts); unsupported versions return {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Protocol 1 is accepted_receipts_v1, contract in vendor/protocol-1.md: identity=(account_id, delivery_id) so the same delivery_id under different accounts is a separate delivery and a batch may mix any number of accounts; accept earliest occurred_at UTC instant, ties -> smallest record_id by code point, accepted keep original fields/order. Timestamps parsed via parse_instant() (RFC3339, Z or numeric offset, compared as UTC). Public suites name protocols explicitly; run python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/<file>.json. Source: issues trial-vbm and trial-dvi, vendor/protocol-1.md.
